review.summary: Phase 22 chunk "typed-connections" delivers a disciplined, strictly additive management 0.86.0 model layer and all five of attempt 1's findings are genuinely fixed in source, not just in prose. I verified vendor fidelity field-for-field against the hash-pinned YAML (MultiTurnClientSessionConfig at mp-openapi.yaml:3257-3264, the two Vertex components at :6174-6233), that the three new models are confined to a dedicated generated `red_team_management` namespace, that the two union extensions are appended tails with byte-identical legacy prefixes (generated.rs:172267-172272, :172554-172561) and that the only four frozen graph nodes touched are the two unions plus the two schema-bound enums. The new enum values land on the schema-bound `TargetCreateRequest*` types (generated.rs:174704-174705, :174768) with old names, old order and `Unknown(String)` preserved; the frozen TypeScript parity enums stay untouched and now carry rustdoc naming the divergence (:162441, :174151), with a matching `enumCompatibility` block in the overlay ledger. Request-only Vertex patterns are registered in the reviewed allowlist (validation.rs:1063-1066), unregistered sources fail closed (:1219) and the response-mode regex bypass is intact (:1225-1233). Typed projections stay optional, fall back to the raw extension entry on decode failure and skip the duplicate key only when set (generate_models.py:471-506), and the Rust fixtures prove null/number/array/object/string round-trip byte-identically with secrets redacted. The five target response declarations are exercised through a stub transport across 5 providers x 4 auth shapes x 2 response modes x 5 operations with operation-name, method, /mgmt-plane path and model/validator parity assertions, and the synthetic secret never appears in Debug, errors or the transport request. The attempt-1 ownership gap is closed: both Gateway derived-ledger verifiers are now in phases 22-25 and executed, and `--require-through-phase 22` performs real artifact verification (hash-bound overlay/generator/vendor/implementation bytes, union-ledger agreement, 13 named wire tests, rejection of any current live receipt). Evidence is real: the complete 42-command gate ran at the reviewed SHA 20d8e7c6 with every exit code 0, including cargo fmt/check/clippy -D warnings/test/test --examples/doc on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 across both Red Team feature sets, plus a private-material scan executed at that same SHA with zero matches. Remaining deficiencies are real but non-blocking: the plan's milestone 22.3 "package-independent consumer examples" clause has no artifact and no chunk owns crates/scm-sdk/examples; the management attribution lines in both NOTICE files are unasserted by any check; the adoption verifier's required-binding floor omits generated.rs; and the new governance regression hardcodes two ledgers instead of the general assertion that was requested.

findings.description: The plan's phase-22 milestone 3 (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:216-219) requires "Update graph/model/operation ledgers and package-independent consumer examples." The ledgers were updated and regenerated, but no example was. I grepped crates/scm-sdk/examples for profiling_status, VERTEX_AI, client_session and VertexAI and found zero matches across all twelve examples, and no phase-22 chunk scope_evidence list in docs/phase-status.json:5578-5733 includes crates/scm-sdk/examples, so no chunk owns the clause. response_defaults.rs:12-26 is the obvious landing spot: it already drives TargetResponse through both response modes with omission/null parity, yet its payload still contains only pre-0.86.0 connection_params/auth_config shapes, so it demonstrates none of the new union branches, the REALTIME/VERTEX_AI/N8N values, the four typed projections or the profiling filter. The integration suites in crates/scm-sdk/tests do consume only public paths and are compiled by the executed `cargo test --examples`/`cargo test` commands, so the public reachability of the new types is proved; what is missing is the maintainer-facing consumer demonstration the milestone names, and there is no recorded decision deferring it.
findings.required_fix: Either extend an existing offline example (response_defaults.rs is the natural one) to cover a Vertex provider branch, an explicit client_session multi-turn config, a REALTIME response_mode, the four typed projection fields with a raw passthrough fallback, and a TargetListOptions profiling_status filter; or record an explicit reviewed deferral in docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md and docs/phase-status.json stating that the two integration suites satisfy the milestone-3 consumer-example clause. If an example is added, add crates/scm-sdk/examples to the owning chunk's scope_evidence as a new scope revision.

findings.description: NOTICE:12-14 and crates/scm-sdk/NOTICE:12-14 correctly name pan.dev revision 582e30543bf2adfd8b0ee457170d22b5c380dfbe / OpenAPI 0.86.0, satisfying the milestone-2 packaging requirement, and scripts/check-rust.py:117-118 enforces that the packaged copy is byte-identical to the root copy. But no check asserts the content. tools/test_red_team_dataplane.py:27-33 only asserts that the vendor license file's text is contained in both NOTICE files, and the management license (contracts/manifest.json:2032-2042) is the same 1075-byte MIT text as the data-plane one, so that assertion passes with or without the management attribution sentence. tools/red_team_management.py and tools/test_red_team_management.py contain no occurrence of NOTICE at all. The overlay ledger hash-binds root NOTICE (contracts/red-team-management-model-overlay.json:174-177), which detects an unregenerated edit, but regeneration recomputes that digest, so removing lines 12-14 from both files and rerunning the generator would pass the whole phase-22 gate.
findings.required_fix: Add an assertion mirroring tools/test_red_team_dataplane.py:27-33 to tools/test_red_team_management.py or tools/test_red_team_management_models.py that both NOTICE and crates/scm-sdk/NOTICE contain the management COMMIT constant and the pinned OpenAPI version string, and that the pinned license text appears in both.

findings.description: verify_runtime_adoption hash-checks every row present in the overlay's sourceBindings, but the `required` floor at lines 698-703 that prevents a row from being dropped omits crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs, NOTICE and tools/test_red_team_management_models.py, all three of which generate_models.py:1096-1104 does bind today. generated.rs is the single most important runtime artifact of this chunk: it carries both appended union variants (:172270, :172559) and both extended schema-bound enums (:174704-174705, :174768). Dropping it from management_bindings would silently relax the adoption gate, and because generate_models.py is itself bound only to its own recomputed digest the binding list is not self-protecting. The practical exposure is nil while `python tools/generate_models.py --check` stays in the phase command list, since that byte-compares every generated output against regeneration from the pinned inventory plus overlay, which is strictly stronger than a hash binding. This is defense-in-depth consistency rather than an open hole.
findings.required_fix: Add 'crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs', 'NOTICE' and 'tools/test_red_team_management_models.py' to the `required` set at tools/red_team_management.py:698-703, and extend tools/test_red_team_management.py's existing sourceBindings tampering test to assert that removing the generated.rs row fails verify_runtime_adoption.

findings.description: test_gateway_derived_ledgers_keep_their_owning_checks closes the attempt-1 gap for the two named Gateway ledgers across phases 22-25 and additionally cross-checks them against the active phase's declared scope (lines 188-193). But attempt 1's required fix asked for the general invariant: "every contract ledger inside the active phase scope has its generating/verifying tool in that phase's command list." The implementation hardcodes a two-entry `owners` dict, so a future derived ledger added to a chunk scope reproduces exactly the original defect with no test failure. I confirmed the other derived ledgers currently in this chunk's scope are in fact covered (contracts/native-fixtures/schemas.json by tools/schema-oracle.mts --check and tools/model_fixtures.py --check; contracts/native-models.json by generate_models.py --check; native-operations/native-exports/qualification by their own executed tools), so nothing is currently unowned.
findings.required_fix: Replace the hardcoded `owners` dict with a declared artifact-to-owner map (for example a module-level table in tools/check_phase.py covering every contracts/*.json and contracts/native-fixtures/* ledger), and assert that every scope_evidence path in the active phase which resolves to such a ledger has its owning command in commands_for(active phase).

findings.description: docs/reviews/phase-22-attempt-01-fixes.md:20 commits to "Correct human-readable phase spacing; retain machine identifiers with an explicit comment." The prose was corrected (line 593 now reads 'phase 23 must exercise old consumers', line 751 reads 'Phase 23-25 qualification evidence'), but the surviving unspaced machine identifiers at lines 523 ('runtime_adopted_phase22', 'pinned_for_phase22_not_runtime_adopted'), 526 ('phase 22 implements overlay' is prose and correct, but the adjacent identifiers are not annotated) and 606 ('adopted_phase22', 'pending_phase22') carry no comment explaining that they are deliberately stable machine keys rather than unfixed proofreading defects. A future maintainer re-running the proofreading pass has no marker telling them these are intentional and that changing them would break consumers of contracts/airs-active-sources.json and compatibility-decisions.json.
findings.required_fix: Add a short comment above the adoptionState expression at tools/red_team_management.py:523 and the runtimeAdoption expression at line 606 stating that these are stable machine identifiers consumed by downstream artifacts and are intentionally not reformatted, and assert their exact literal values in tools/test_red_team_management.py so a reformat fails.

evidence: All five attempt-1 findings are fixed in source, not just claimed: tools/check_phase.py:179-182 adds both Gateway owner commands to every non-21 management phase; crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs:162441-162442 and :174151-174152 carry the frozen-parity rustdoc, emitted deterministically by tools/generate_models.py:1062-1066 via replace_once; crates/scm-sdk/src/models/red_team_management.rs:243-245 carries the declaration-only redact rationale, emitted at tools/red_team_management_models.py:196-200; tools/red_team_management_models.py:252-253 now derives runtimeEnumExtensions from the applied spec delta instead of hardcoding it; tools/red_team_management.py:702 and tools/generate_models.py:1102 bind crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs bytes.

Vendor fidelity verified directly against the pinned YAML: contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/mp-openapi.yaml:6176-6200 declares exactly the three patterns ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$, ^[a-z0-9-]+$, ^[0-9]+$ with all four fields required, :6220-6225 adds format: password and writeOnly only on the redact variant's customer_sa_email, and :3258-3264 declares type as const/default client_session and not required. The generated models reproduce this exactly (red_team_management.rs:127-138, :246-257, :94-117), and tools/red_team_management_models.py:75-79 refuses to run unless the YAML hashes to 5fbb533b... and the normalized JSON equals the parsed YAML.

Union extensions are append-only with verified prefixes: generated.rs:172267-172272 keeps Variant1/Variant2 then adds Variant3(MultiTurnClientSessionConfig), and :172554-172561 keeps Variant1-Variant4 then adds Variant5(VertexAIConnectionParams); both retain #[serde(untagged)], #[non_exhaustive] and Unknown(JsonValue). tools/red_team_management_models.py:170-173 fails closed if a legacy prefix length changes, :225-241 trims only the exact reviewed tail before delegating to the strict frozen comparison so contracts/native-union-variants.json stays byte-frozen, and test_union_extension_verifier_preserves_exact_legacy_prefix exercises prefix-swap, tail-tamper and missing-tail rejection.

Only the schema-bound enums gained values: generated.rs:174692-174707 appends VERTEXAI/N8N to TargetCreateRequestConnectionType (schema s012061) and :174763-174770 appends REALTIME to TargetCreateRequestResponseMode (s012067), both keeping every old variant name, order, as_str mapping and Unknown(String). The frozen parity enums ResponseMode (:162443-162449) and TargetConnectionType (:174153-174166) are unchanged. crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_models.rs:120-132 proves s012061 accepts VERTEX_AI/N8N and rejects REALTIME while s012067 accepts REALTIME, and :135-163 proves the new named variants resolve, unrelated strings stay Unknown, and the frozen constants still return Unknown for VERTEX_AI/REALTIME.

Request-only pattern enforcement with intact response tolerance: crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1063-1066 adds exactly the three reviewed Vertex sources to the registry, :1219 fails closed on an unregistered regex source, and :1225-1233 preserves the pre-existing response-mode bypass for regex/format checks only. red_team_management_models.rs:18-40 proves each bad pattern is rejected in Mode::Request yet preserved byte-exactly in both response modes for both the normal and redact models, while a wrong JSON type is still rejected in response mode.

Typed projections cannot narrow previously accepted payloads: tools/generate_models.py:471-473 raises unless every vendorProjection field is optional; :485-496 removes the key, attempts a typed decode and reinserts the original value as an extension on failure; :500-506 emits the typed field when set and skips the duplicate extension key only in that case. red_team_management_models.rs:96-117 drives null/9/["secret"]/{"secret":...}/"fixture" through both projection families in all three modes with byte-identical round-trips and no secret in Debug, and red_team_management_contracts.rs:559-588 proves Patch::Value overrides a raw collision while Patch::Unset restores the original raw object exactly.

The five target response declarations are exercised end to end: red_team_management_contracts.rs:338-445 drives 5 provider shapes x 4 auth shapes x 2 response modes x 5 operations through a stub transport, asserting operation names (red_team.targets.get/create/update/probe/update_profile), HTTP methods, exact /mgmt-plane paths, typed-serialization equality with validation::parse output, that the replies queue is fully consumed, and that the synthetic secret appears in neither the Debug of the response nor of the transport request (:297). tools/red_team_management.py:636-674 independently records per-row vendor field coverage, requiredness agreement and declared-nullable acceptance against the retained shared root, with an explicit comparisonLimit disclaiming full JSON Schema equivalence.

Defaults, omission/null and discriminator behaviour are preserved: tools/red_team_management_models.py:118-122 emits a bare ZodLiteral for the client_session const and never its vendor default; test_default_is_not_injected_into_client_session and test_runtime_changes_are_only_reviewed_nodes_and_two_unions assert no ZodDefault node is added and that exactly {s012061, s012067, s010462, s010504} change; the executed response_defaults.py --check reports the unchanged 23 default bindings; red_team_management_contracts.rs:158-172 proves ResponseWithoutDefaults round-trips an explicit-null payload byte-identically while Mode::Response still injects ws_response_timeout 110 and basic_auth_location HEADER; :128-156 proves an unknown multi-turn discriminator and a wrong-typed or missing required Vertex field stay rejected rather than being rescued by the Unknown fallback.

Executed evidence matches the reviewed source and the documented gate: docs/reviews/phase-22-chunk-typed-connections-attempt-02.checks.json records phase 22, source_sha256 20d8e7c62e9724cdb945362809f4622a3eca186e3e145c009a469be41c43c5cf, source_unchanged true, passed true and exactly 42 commands all with exit_code 0 and timeout false, matching the 42-command/37-command-subset figures documented at docs/CI.md:159-162. Included are the two newly added Gateway owner checks (operations 61, independentCases 12, zodParses 74; gatewayPhaseSixMethods 194), red_team_management.py --check --require-through-phase 22, generate_models.py --check (19 outputs, 13018 graph nodes), response_defaults.py (23 bindings), the 9 new test_red_team_management_models tests, and five scripts/check-rust.py runs on 1.89.0/1.99.0 covering red-team and red-team,serde_json/arbitrary_precision with fmt, check --all-targets --locked, clippy -D warnings, test, test --examples and doc all at exit 0.

The phase-22 gate is a real implementation gate rather than a registration: tools/red_team_management.py:755-760 requires manifest usedForGeneration true, then verify_runtime_adoption (:691-719) hash-checks the overlay generator, vendor YAML, and every declared binding, requires the two union ledgers to agree, re-verifies the frozen union pin digest, requires every publicModel sid to exist in the runtime graph, and requires all 13 MANAGEMENT_WIRE_TESTS function names to exist in the contracts file (all 13 confirmed present at red_team_management_contracts.rs:52-559); build() at :595-599 also invokes it unconditionally whenever adoption is declared. verify_offline_live_boundary (:726-740) rejects any contracts/live-evidence.json, any non-null liveReceipt and any row whose liveAcceptance is not 'unverified', and the executed native_operations/native_exports/qualification checks report liveVerified 0 with 448 operations unverified.

Attribution and ownership are complete for publication: NOTICE:10-15 and crates/scm-sdk/NOTICE:10-15 both name pan.dev revision 582e30543bf2adfd8b0ee457170d22b5c380dfbe / OpenAPI 0.86.0 alongside the data-plane revision, scripts/check-rust.py:117-118 makes byte-equality of the two copies a pass condition (enforced in all five executed runs), and contracts/manifest.json:1949-1963 plus :2442-2480 carry full source and vendorArtifact ownership with usedForGeneration true, matching license pan-dev-582e30543bf2 and exact per-artifact digests that the executed verify-contracts.py --self-test covers with 27 rejected tampering cases including unowned-vendor-file, modified-vendor-file, vendor-symlink and duplicate-source-id.

The phase-21 residual review-gate defect in this chunk's scope is fixed: tools/review_phase.py:155 now accepts a phase keyword and :194 forwards it, and both verify_record call sites (:270 and :279-280) pass phase=phase, so the phase-aware floor can no longer be bypassed by a mutually inconsistent decision/gate_passed pair. check_evidence (:201-218) still requires the chunk's checks file to carry scope None, passed true, the matching source digest and a command list exactly equal to commands_for(22) with every exit code 0, which the attempt-02 receipt satisfies.

Private-material evidence was actually executed at this source: docs/checks/phase-22-private-material.json records sourceSha256 20d8e7c6..., headCommit 69d9ea2b, sourceUnchanged true, 1952 git-visible files, 0 selected credential matches, 133 published-crate source/example candidates with 0 registration-value matches, 3 pre-existing unchanged tenant-identifier occurrences with 0 new or changed, and five explicit limitations; the gate's --check reported receiptFresh true with privateScanReexecuted false, which the receipt itself discloses at limitation 5.
limitations: Read-only review: I executed nothing and cannot recompute SHA256 digests. The reviewed-source digest 20d8e7c62e9724cdb945362809f4622a3eca186e3e145c009a469be41c43c5cf and the checks-file digest a1554d15ada174bd3a7f8d7d7adbb2f3f65ec455dc2495da8840c6905f499307 are accepted as supplied; I corroborated the source digest only through the self-consistent source_sha256/source_unchanged fields in the checks file and the independently written docs/checks/phase-22-private-material.json, which records the same digest and a matching timestamp window.

scripts/check-rust.py receipts record each cargo command and its exit code, not per-test names or counts, so I cannot confirm from the receipt alone which individual Rust tests executed. I confirmed that both feature sets which compile the two #![cfg(feature = "red-team")] integration files were among the executed combinations on both toolchains, and that cargo test --examples ran, but not that any specific test function was reached.

Generated model correctness was assessed through selected declarations, the vendor source, the deterministic generator and the passing byte-exact generate_models.py --check, not by reading all 174k+ lines of crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs. I inspected the four changed node families (two union enums, two schema-bound enums), the two frozen parity enums and the three new management models in full; other generated output is covered only by the executed regeneration comparison.

The five target response declarations are evidenced by a field-presence/requiredness/nullability comparison against the retained shared root plus the bound Rust fixture matrix, not by a field-complete type-level matrix derived separately from TargetSchema and TargetRedactSchema. tools/red_team_management.py:671 states this limit explicitly and the plan defers the full changed-schema matrix to phase 23, so I did not score its absence.

Reviewed the typed-connections chunk scope only. crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/targets.rs (target-filtering) and docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md plus the validation-graph/G25 report ownership (connection-compatibility) were inspected only where needed to judge this chunk's models, ledgers and gates; the profiling-filter rustdoc and the G25 management projection table belong to sibling chunks and are not scored here.

Two observable behaviour changes for existing consumers are sanctioned by the plan rather than by this chunk's tests and are therefore recorded here, not as findings: pure-Vertex and explicitly tagged client_session payloads transition from Unknown(JsonValue) or a validation failure to the new named Variant5/Variant3 branches (source-compatible only because both enums are #[non_exhaustive]), and the four formerly extension-visible keys basic_username, basic_password, audio_request_json and audio_curl now move out of the extensions map into typed fields whenever they decode. The plan assigns disclosure of both to the phase 24 changelog.

No live, network or tenant verification exists or is claimed for this chunk, and the gate actively rejects any current live receipt, so nothing here establishes upstream acceptance of the new variants, enum values or the profiling filter; the declared credential-bearing response shapes are test requirements, not evidence that a live server returns plaintext secrets.

I did not inspect credential or tenant-registration material, anything outside this repository, or docs/research beyond what phase-status residual findings quoted; .local/typescript was touched only through the recorded check invocations, not read directly.
